title: Integrated Attachment Theory
summary:
This pilot randomized waitlist-controlled study will evaluate the feasibility and preliminary effects of a 12-week Integrated Attachment Theory (IAT) psychoeducational coaching program in adults ages 18-65 with an insecure attachment pattern identified through study screening.

Eligible participants will be randomized 1:1 to immediate IAT or a 12-week waitlist followed by IAT. The immediate group will complete in-person Boston University assessments before and after IAT; the waitlist group will complete assessments at baseline, after the 12-week waiting period, and after subsequently completing IAT.

The primary objectives are to determine whether the study procedures and intervention are feasible and to estimate the magnitude and variability of pre/post changes. The investigators hypothesize that IAT will be associated with improvement in attachment-related patterns, emotion regulation, interpersonal functioning, and well-being, together with changes in physiological and cortical responses during attachment-related emotion regulation compared with the waitlist period.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Speak and read English sufficiently to complete study questionnaires and the IAT program
* Meets the PDS attachment-style eligibility criterion for insecure attachment
* Able and willing to attend required in-person Boston University (BU) research visits
* Able and willing, if assigned, to participate in the 12-week remote IAT program.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Self-reported neurological disorder or condition
* Self-reported psychiatric/mental-health disorder
* Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) total score \>14
* Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) total score \>14
* Failure to meet the PDS attachment-style eligibility criterion
* Inability to complete required study procedures
* A safety concern that makes participation inappropriate.
